sections.title: Visual arts
sections.content:
Vocabulary for discussing art and artistic expression:
• masterpiece — an outstanding work of art. The painting is considered a masterpiece of Renaissance art.
• abstract — not representing reality directly. Abstract art focuses on shapes, colours, and emotions rather than objects.
• avant-garde — experimental and innovative in art. The gallery specialises in avant-garde installations.
• aesthetic — concerned with beauty and artistic taste. The building has great aesthetic appeal.
• contemporary — belonging to the present time. Contemporary art often challenges traditional boundaries.

sections.title: Creative process
sections.content:
How creative work develops:
• inspiration — a sudden creative idea. Nature was a constant source of inspiration for the poet.
• improvise — create spontaneously without preparation. Jazz musicians often improvise during performances.
• collaborate — work together on a creative project. The two artists collaborated on a stunning mural.
• refine — improve by making small changes. She spent months refining her novel before publishing.
• versatile — able to work across many styles. A versatile artist can paint, sculpt, and draw equally well.

sections.title: Criticism and reception
sections.content:
How art is received and evaluated:
• critique — a detailed analysis and assessment. The art critic wrote a harsh critique of the exhibition.
• acclaimed — publicly praised. The film was critically acclaimed and won several awards.
• provocative — intended to stimulate strong reactions. The provocative sculpture sparked heated public debate.
• derivative — imitative of another artist's work. Critics dismissed the paintings as derivative and unoriginal.

exercises.question: Art that doesn't represent real objects but uses shapes and colours is:
exercises.explanation: Abstract art uses shapes, colours, and forms to achieve its effect rather than depicting recognisable objects.

exercises.question: A work of art considered to be the finest ever created is a:
exercises.explanation: A masterpiece is a work of outstanding artistry or skill.

exercises.question: Art that is experimental and pushes boundaries is:
exercises.hint: Ahead of its time, breaking rules.
exercises.explanation: Avant-garde describes new and experimental ideas in art, especially in the arts.

exercises.question: Work that copies another artist's style without originality is:
exercises.explanation: Derivative means imitative of the work of another person, and usually disapproved of for that reason.

exercises.question: Creating something spontaneously without planning is to:
exercises.explanation: To improvise means to create and perform spontaneously without preparation.

exercises.question: A work of art that is publicly praised and celebrated is:
Concerned with beauty and the appreciation of beauty is:
exercises.hint: Related to visual appeal and taste.
exercises.explanation: Aesthetic relates to the appreciation of beauty or good taste.

exercises.question: Art intended to cause strong reactions or controversy is:
exercises.explanation: Provocative means deliberately causing a strong reaction, especially anger or debate.
